description.value: The study used structural MRI and resting-state fMRI patterns with Gaussian process classifiers to distinguish medication-free depressed subjects with major depressive disorder from those with bipolar disorder and to examine the influence of mood state.

spans.text: In the current study, we used sMRI and RS-fMRI data (connectivity of the DMN, left and right FPN, and SN) to examine the discriminative potential of Gaussian process classifier (GPC)-based pattern recognition analysis in subjects with MDD and BD.

spans.text: For each RSN and for gray matter volume, the following classification problems were defined: MDDd vs BDd, and MDDr vs BDr.
As we were the first to classify currently medication-free MDD and BD, and also to classify remitted subjects (except one study in medicated samples 26 ), this study was explorative.

The GPC was able to predict diagnostic group based on patterns of DMN connectivity and of gray matter volume but only for the depressed state (Table 2 ).
Statistical significance was determined by permutation testing.
The GPC provided probabilistic predictions for each diagnostic category for each subject.
accuracy

DMN functional connectivity patterns distinguished subjects with MDDd from subjects with BDd with 69.1% accuracy ( P =.02; sensitivity 70.0%; specificity 68.2%; positive predictive value 50.0%; negative predictive value 83.3%).
We used a leave-one-out cross-validation strategy to estimate the generalization ability of our classifier.

value: DMN functional connectivity patterns distinguished subjects with MDDd from subjects with BDd with 69.1% accuracy (P=.02).
DMN connectivity can be used to discriminate between MDD and BD in the depressed state; by contrast, remitted patient groups could not be distinguished.

model_settings.value: Binary Gaussian process classifiers implemented in the Pattern Recognition for Neuroimaging Toolbox (PRoNTo); features were restricted to gray-matter voxels within each RSN mask or an emotion-regulation mask; hyper-parameter set by maximizing model evidence under a Gaussian approximation using Type II maximum likelihood; leave-one-out cross-validation; probabilistic predictions converted to categorical predictions using a threshold based on training-set class frequencies; balanced accuracy used for imbalanced groups; significance assessed by permutation testing.
